questions.question: Day 7 Practice (Weekend Plans & Weather): When talking about tidying up the room (this evening), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The cab driver'?

options.a: I am tidying up the room right now.
options.b: He is tidy up room.
options.c: I was tidying up the room right now.
options.d: I am tidy up room.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I am tidying up the room right now.".

questions.question: Day 7 Vocabulary (Weekend Plans & Weather): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'reach out to'?

options.a: Contact someone for help or information.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'reach out to' means: contact someone for help or information. Example: "I will reach out to customer support tomorrow."

questions.question: Day 7 Terms (Weekend Plans & Weather): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'circle back':

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: Return to a topic later for follow-up.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'circle back' means: return to a topic later for follow-up. Example: "Let us circle back to the timeline discussion."

questions.question: Day 7 Vocabulary (Weekend Plans & Weather): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'follow up'?

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 1 (Weekend Plans & Weather):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.d: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 2 (Weekend Plans & Weather):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.d: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 3 (Weekend Plans & Weather):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.
options.b: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 4 (Weekend Plans & Weather):

Telugu: "సాయంత్రం మా ఇంటికి రండి, టీ తాగుదాం."
(Literal attempt: "Evening my house come, tea drink.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Evening my house come, tea drink.
options.c: I am needing to evening my house come, tea drink.
options.d: Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together."

Use 'drop by our home' for informal invitations.
